source.title: The loss surface and expressivity of deep convolutional neural networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no relevant section appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes CNN expressivity and loss landscapes, and discusses random-label fitting, but it does not test the claim's training behavior or any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for experiments fitting random labels and noise; those cited results are not this study's results. Its MNIST experiment uses the true labels and varies filter count, so it does not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper proves finite-sample expressivity and conditional loss-landscape results, but neither establishes stochastic-gradient convergence on random labels nor measures any listed version. Its experiment uses true MNIST labels; random-label fitting results are attributed to Zhang et al.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish finite-sample expressivity and conditional zero-loss landscape results for sufficiently wide CNNs, and suggest these help explain effective training. They do not prove stochastic-gradient convergence or report their own random-label experiments. Cross-entropy is explicitly outside their analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theoretical expressivity and loss-landscape results for CNNs, plus an MNIST true-label experiment; it does not reproduce the random-label training procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical results depend on width, architecture, activation-function assumptions, and, for the loss-landscape result, a fully connected layer after the wide layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollary 3.6 proves exact representability of arbitrary scalar targets on finite training samples under the stated data, activation, and architecture assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CNNs satisfying these assumptions with last-hidden-layer width at least the training-set size have universal finite-sample expressivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.5 establishes zero-loss global minima and global optimality of every critical point within S_k under its architectural assumptions. With analytic activations through the wide layer, the complement of S_k has measure zero. This provides no training-time or convergence guarantee.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the specified wide CNNs with a fully connected layer immediately after the wide layer, every critical point within S_k is globally optimal for squared loss.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (venue stated in supplied metadata; paper text also identifies ICML 2018 proceedings)
record.problems: The random-label and noise-fitting experiments are cited from prior work, not performed here. The MNIST experiment concerns true labels and does not report random-label results. The paper's optimization theorem is conditional on a particular architecture and loss setup.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The MNIST table reports true-label training and test errors while varying filter count, which does not measure any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Stochastic-gradient fitting of completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Training to zero error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs. Tiny Gaussian perturbations to MNIST do not test these conditions.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and generalization with true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 is already declared in rows_left_out and uses true labels. A full-measure parameter set does not itself guarantee that optimization avoids excluded critical points. The supplied paper identifies its venue as ICML 2018, correcting the record's ICLR metadata.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks trained with stochastic gradient methods fit random labels, achieve chance test error, and do so without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time for random versus true labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across corruption fractions, including whether test error rises steadily toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.

rows.subject: standard CNN satisfying the conditions of Theorem 3.4
rows.size_stated: last hidden layer wider than the number of training samples
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical finite-sample expressivity result: establishes existence of parameters that fit any scalar-valued target on a finite training set exactly.

conditions.value: Theorem 3.4 conditions at the last hidden layer

rows.measure: training outputs match arbitrary scalar-valued finite-sample targets
rows.value: For every target y ∈ R^N, there exists a parameter choice with f_L(x_i) = y_i for every i ∈ [N].
rows.note: This is an existence result, not evidence that stochastic gradient training reaches the solution or that the architecture and training setup match the claim's original settings.
rows.check: Corollary 3.6 correctly establishes existence of parameters fitting arbitrary scalar targets under its assumptions. It does not establish that stochastic-gradient training finds them. The reported observed state describes expressivity, not an effect named by a claim version. The width condition permits equality: n_(L−1) ≥ N.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
